summary: CBS Sports previews the Nov. 25, 2023 super middleweight fight between David Benavidez (27-0, 23 KOs) and Demetrius Andrade (32-0, 19 KOs) at Michelob Ultra Arena in Las Vegas. Both unbeaten fighters hope a win will earn a shot at Canelo Alvarez, and the piece covers their backgrounds, quotes, odds and the undercard. Brian Campbell picks Benavidez by unanimous decision over 12 rounds, citing his pressure and busier, come-forward style.
one_line: Preview of unbeaten David Benavidez vs. Demetrius Andrade on Nov. 25, 2023 in Las Vegas, with odds, undercard and a Benavidez UD12 pick.
key_facts: Demetrius Andrade is 32-0 with 19 KOs, is 35 years old, and is a former two-division champion and 2008 U.S. Olympian from Rhode Island.
David Benavidez is 26 years old, 27-0 with 23 KOs, and a former two-time super middleweight titleholder born in Arizona to parents of Mexican and Ecuadorian descent.
The fight is a 168-pound bout on Saturday, Nov. 25 at Michelob Ultra Arena at Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas, on Showtime PPV priced at $74.99, with a 9 p.m. ET start listed in the info box.
Odds: Benavidez -440 vs. Andrade +335; Andrade is roughly a 3-1 underdog.
Benavidez beat Caleb Plant by decision in March, wearing him out over 12 rounds; Benavidez says this is the final Showtime pay-per-view.
Benavidez became the youngest champion in divisional history at 20 in 2017, and was twice stripped of his WBC title: once for a failed cocaine test and once mid-pandemic for missing weight.

Andrade signed with Al Haymon's Premier Boxing Champions in late 2022 and won a wide decision over Demond Nicholson in his super middleweight debut in January, on the Gervonta Davis-Hector Luis Garcia card.
Andrade is a lengthy southpaw who relies on speed, guile and elite defense; his power is accumulative rather than one-punch, and he says 'I'm not Caleb Plant.'
Andrade had chased Canelo Alvarez, Gennadiy Golovkin and Jermall Charlo without landing those fights, and said he considered walking away multiple times.
Benavidez says he has been the mandatory fighter for two years, having won a title eliminator and then the WBC interim title, and is frustrated that the Alvarez fight hasn't happened.
Co-feature: WBC middleweight champion Jermall Charlo (-700) returns from a layoff since June 2021 against Jose Benavidez Jr. (+500), David's older brother, in a 10-round non-title bout.
Other undercard bouts: Subriel Matias -350 vs. Shohjahon Ergashev +275, and Hector Luis Garcia -290 vs. Lamont Roach +235.
Brian Campbell's pick is Benavidez via UD12, arguing Andrade's best hope otherwise is a moral victory by going the distance.
